name: Nova Orchestrator
tag: Runs a team of AI agents on your work, hands tasks between them and shows progress in one place.

scenarios.title: Onboard new clients
scenarios.ask: We sign about {clients} new clients a month. Run onboarding with agents, with a person approving the {approval}.
steps: Collects company details and goals from a short form and checks for missing fields.
Fills the contract template and routes it for approval.
Creates the client folder, project board and shared channel once the contract is signed.
Drafts the kickoff agenda and proposes three meeting times.
Shows each client's stage, waiting time and who holds the next step.
followups: What happens if an approval sits too long?
The Tracker reminds the approver after one business day and shows the delay on the board, so nothing waits quietly.
Can we add our own steps?
Yes. Each step is an agent with an input, an output and an owner. You add a step and choose where it hands off.
You can. It is safer for new flows but slower. Many teams start with every step and relax it once the agents have a track record.

scenarios.title: Run a content pipeline
scenarios.ask: Produce {pieces} articles a week with research, drafting, editing and publishing agents.
steps: Builds a brief for each article with sources and key points.
Checks facts against the brief, tone and length, and sends weak drafts back once.
Formats and schedules approved articles after an editor signs off.
Shows each article's stage and flags any stuck more than a day.
followups: A person approves every article before it publishes. The agents prepare the work, they do not publish on their own.
What if research finds nothing useful?
The Research agent marks the brief as thin and the Tracker holds the article for a human decision instead of passing it on.

scenarios.title: Unstick stalled work
scenarios.ask: We have {agents} agents running and {tasks} tasks in flight. Some are stuck. Find where and fix the handoffs.
steps: Found {=max(1, round(tasks * 0.12))} tasks idle for more than 24 hours.
{=max(1, round(tasks * 0.07))} of them wait on a handoff that has no receiving agent after a recent change.
Proposed new handoff rules for {=max(1, ceil(agents / 4))} agents to close the gaps.
Replays the stuck tasks once you approve the new rules.
followups: Usually an agent is renamed or its output changes shape, so the next agent no longer accepts it. The Orchestrator checks this whenever an agent changes.
No. Each task has an ID and the Supervisor skips steps that already finished.
